4.x: **Language:** Hoysala inscriptions are mostly in **Kannada** (some Sanskrit); Kannada literature flourished in both Jain and Virashaiva streams.
**Religion:** Jainism (Gangaraja, queen **Shantala Devi**), **Sri Vaishnavism** (Ramanuja at **Melukote / Tirunarayanapuram**), Shaivism and Virashaivism all had royal patronage.
**Madhvacharya** (1238–1317), founder of **Dvaita**, was born near **Udupi** in Hoysala times; his math at Udupi worships Krishna.

**Temple carving signature:** sculptors **signed their work**; friezes run **elephants (lowest) → lions / horsemen → scrolls → epic scenes**; **Darpana Sundari** (lady with a mirror) is the famous Belur madanika.
